answer: One identity, one tidal creek. The miner sinks a pressure gauge on a trellis of stakes, filing six weeks of readings. The verifier matches phase lag and amplitude to the nearest official gauge: two accounts whose curves beat within four minutes fold into one vote, since the same tide is behind them. It also files chlorophyll from a sealed fluorometer; a dead ditch shows the wrong pigment and fails. Gauges cost $2,900; a coastline holds maybe 300 distinct lags, so a thousand sybils need a thousand creeks that do not exist. Water keeps its own clock; you cannot rent a second estuary.
